thread:
omar: Heads-up — saw weird cold-start spike on a mixed-seqlen workload. KV cache reuse drops to 12% briefly, then recovers. Trace attached in perfetto but TL;DR: prefetch policy seems to preemptively evict hot prefixes when a long sequence arrives.
sara: Hmm that matches the nsys timeline I grabbed. Kernel handoff jumps from fast-quant path to fallback GEMM for ~120ms, then lots of redispatch.
kevin: Can you paste the nsys command you ran?
omar: `nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda --sample=cpu --output=adaptive_prefetch --complete-tool-report true --target-processes all`
luis: I see two things in the capture: 1) batching heuristic groups a long request with many short ones, increasing kv cache working set; 2) scheduler chooses a kernel variant based on median seqlen, not tail, so the long request forces a kernel switch mid-batch.
mei: Did you get kernel symbols? I saw symbolized stack frames pointing at `select_kernel_variant()` and `dispatch_gemm_fallback()` in the hot path.
omar: Yup — perfetto shows repeated calls to `evict_prefix_range()` right after `prefetch_prefixes()` for same session. Looks like prefetch affinity causes immediate eviction when memory pressure spikes.
sara: Reaction: :thinking_face: Could be the soft-affinity heuristic aiming to co-locate similar seqlens but mis-classifies mixed batches. Maybe lower the affinity threshold or delay prefetch for long inflight batches.
kevin: Quick experiment idea: flip SOFT_AFFINITY from 0.8 -> 0.5 and run a 1k sample. Also try `PREFETCH_DELAY_MS=8` to give batching a chance.
luis: And enable prefix shadowing metric — add `KV_CACHE_SHADOW=1` to the agent to log prefetch/evict pairs so we can correlate.
infra-bot: Deploy started: feature/trace-adaptive-prefetch -> canary on x86-gpu-pool (2 nodes). CI: nsys capture enabled.
mei: After the canary run (10k requests), reuse went from 15% -> 33% and p95 latency improved 18% on the mixed workload. Kernel switches dropped by ~60%.
omar: Good signal. Next steps: tune soft-affinity heuristic to use weighted tail percentile (90th) instead of median, and add backpressure to prefetch when dispatch queue > 64.
sara: I'll open a PR with the config and small unit test for the shadow logging.
kevin: Also add a short perfetto bookmark export to the incident template so we can attach slices in future.
mei: Thanks all — saved a bunch of noisy evictions. Follow-up: capture one more nsys with memstats and send to perf team for kernel selection improvements.
